title: Void Ending in a Trine to Pluto
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The trine is the best of the aspects, the one the doctrine uses to tie the Moon to the fortunes. The text grades it as perfect friendship, because the signs it joins are of one element and gaze at each other in full agreement; works meant to endure are founded with the Moon fixed, and the lord of her house regarding her in trine or sextile.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a trine to Pluto, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his buried endings. Pluto is unknown to Picatrix, found in 1930 and outside the world the book describes at every point. Any reading of it here is this almanac's extension of Picatrix's doctrine, never the source's own words. Named for the Roman lord of the underworld, it is read as the far, dark hinge of the set: a course that closes on it ends in the buried kind of ending, the small death of a matter before the next sign begins.
